description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:426:

    pub struct Verifier<'a, V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher> {
        anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
        sig_verifier: &'a V,
        rev_checker: &'a R,
        policy: &'a ValidationPolicy,
        aia: &'a A,
    }

The three trait generics V/R/A are named in the public type. Every caller spelling `Verifier<'_, V, R, A>` (or even `Verifier<'_, DefaultVerifier, NoRevocation, NoAiaFetcher>`) — including the workspace's own tests — depends on the three-generic shape.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CALLER:

The workspace's stated architectural model (AGENTS.md crate-stack description for pkix-chain): "A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher 3rd generic is the third trust-domain callback alongside SignatureVerifier (signatures) and RevocationChecker (revocation)". This is the **complete** trust-domain seam *as currently conceived*. But the workspace also has live skeleton crates for adjacent trust-domain concerns:

- `pkix-ct` (RFC 6962 SCT verification) — naturally wants a per-cert `LogVerifier`-style callback to decide whether an SCT chain is acceptable for the active anchors.
- `pkix-dane` (RFC 6698 TLSA matching) — naturally wants a `TlsaLookup`-style callback.
- `pkix-composite` (PQC composite signatures) — naturally wants extended verifier dispatch.

Any of these landing on `Verifier` is a breaking change to the public generic list. Callers update from `Verifier<'_, V, R>` to `Verifier<'_, V, R, A, C>` (or whatever shape) and every wrapper signature changes.

This is the canonical "trait bounds on public methods that constrain callers to specific upstream implementations" leakage shape from the slash-command checklist. The fix shapes are well-known:

(a) **Builder/configurator pattern.** `Verifier::new(anchors, policy).with_signature_verifier(V).with_revocation(R).with_aia(A).build()`. New seams add new `.with_*` methods; the type stays `Verifier<'a>` (or a `Verifier<'a, Phase>` if you want typestate). Adding a 4th seam is non-breaking.

(b) **Single bundled trait.** `pub trait ChainBackend { type Verifier; type Revocation; type Aia; ... }` and `Verifier<'a, B: ChainBackend>`. Adding an associated type to `ChainBackend` IS breaking, but it relocates the change to ONE trait the caller has likely impl'd just once.

(c) **Type-state separation.** A single Verifier owning trait-object refs (`&'a dyn SignatureVerifier`, etc.) loses static dispatch (a real cost for the hot signature-verify path) but presents a stable signature.

The doctest at lines 47-63 already commits to `Verifier::new_no_aia(...)` returning a `Verifier<'_, &DefaultVerifier, &NoRevocation>`-shaped type — so a refactor to (a) or (b) needs to keep this construction shape working.

PRE-1.0 FRAMING (AGENTS.md): breaking changes are free; architectural completeness is the target. Picking (a) or (b) now costs one breaking-change minor bump and forecloses on the lock-in. Shipping `Verifier<'a, V, R, A>` at 1.0 means future trust-domain seams require a 2.0.

This is closely related to PKIX-sqek.4 (wrappers cannot opt into AIA) — fixing the wrapper-genericity issue surfaces the same shape question on the wrapper functions. A unified shape for both moves the right way.

Filed as priority 1 because the cost of getting it wrong post-1.0 is a major version bump across the entire crate stack.
title: Verifier exposes three named trait generics (V, R, A) — adding a 4th trust-domain seam later breaks every caller
